title: Verbal Adverbs 5: The Same-Subject Rule
description: The most important constraint on Russian verbal adverbs: the gerund and the main verb must share a subject. Today: spotting dangling-gerund errors and rewriting them with когда clauses.
descriptionRussian: Главное ограничение русского деепричастия: оно и главный глагол должны иметь общий субъект. Сегодня: распознавание ошибки висячего деепричастия и переход к конструкции с когда.
intro: One hard constraint governs both forms: whoever performs the main verb must also perform the verbal adverb. Break it and you get the Russian equivalent of a dangling modifier, where the rain approaches the house. The fix is always the same, which is to rewrite the clause with a joining word that can carry its own subject.
rules: A verbal adverb must share a subject with the main verb. The gerund's action is performed by whoever performs the main action.
The dangling-gerund error happens when the gerund attaches to a phantom subject: *Подходя к дому, начался дождь (I approach, but the rain starts: two subjects).
The standard fix for a dangling gerund is to rewrite as a когда clause, which carries its own subject: Когда я подходил к дому, начался дождь.
Keep the main clause's own subject in place when you rewrite: the rain still starts (начался дождь); only the gerund moves into the когда clause.
The rule applies regardless of gerund position. A gerund can come BEFORE or AFTER the main clause and still demand the same subject.
examples: Гуляя по парку, мы говорили о работе. (Same subject: мы. Correct.)
Прочитав книгу, она лежала на диване. (Same subject: она. Correct.)
*Подходя к дому, начался дождь. (Different subjects: I approach, but the rain starts. Wrong.)
Когда я подходил к дому, начался дождь. (Когда clause carries its own subject. Correct.)
*Открывая дверь, упала ваза. (Different subjects: I open, but the vase falls. Wrong.)
Маша закрыла окно, выйдя на улицу. (Same subject: Маша. Gerund after main clause. Correct.)

items.prompt: Recap from L3: what is the perfective verbal adverb of закончить?
items.promptEnglish: Form the perfective gerund of закончить.
items.hint: Drop -ть from the perfective infinitive. Add the suffix.
items.explanation: Recap: закончить → закончи- + в → закончив. Заканчивая is the imperfective gerund of заканчивать (the aspect partner); закончить is the infinitive; закончил is the finite past. We need this form to anchor today's same-subject drills.

items.prompt: In 'Зная город, Маша легко нашла дорогу', who performs BOTH actions?
items.promptEnglish: Whose subject is shared by зная and нашла?
items.hint: Find the subject of the main verb (нашла). The gerund must share that subject.
items.explanation: Маша is the subject of нашла, and per the same-subject rule, she also performs зная. The city is not knowing; the road is not knowing. Both verbs answer to Маша.

items.promptEnglish: Which sentence has a single shared subject for both verbs?
items.hint: Check each option: do both verbs answer to the same noun?
items.explanation: Only 'Открывая окно, я почувствовал ветер' has a single subject (я) for both verbs. The other three break the same-subject rule: the phone is not reading; the vase is not approaching; the snow is not saying hello.

items.promptEnglish: Which sentence breaks the same-subject rule?
options: Гуляя по парку, мы говорили о работе.
items.hint: Find the option whose two verbs have different subjects.
items.explanation: In 'Прочитав статью, телефон зазвонил,' the implicit reader (я) reads the article, but the phone is what rings. The subject of прочитав (the speaker) and зазвонил (телефон) differ: a dangling gerund. The other three options have a single shared subject.

items.prompt: Which is the correct когда rewrite of '*Открывая дверь, упала ваза'?
items.promptEnglish: How do you fix the dangling-gerund error?
options: Когда я открывал дверь, упала ваза.
Открывая дверь, упала ваза с полки.
items.answer: Когда я открывал дверь, упала ваза.
items.hint: The когда clause should restore the human subject (я) that the dangling gerund left implicit.
items.explanation: The fix supplies the missing subject (я) inside a finite когда clause. The vase's falling stays in the main clause with its own subject (ваза). The second option uses an awkward reflexive that loses the speaker; the third option keeps the broken gerund; the fourth option swaps to a perfective gerund without fixing the subject mismatch.

items.prompt: Is 'Маша закрыла окно, выйдя на улицу' grammatical?
options: No, the gerund must come BEFORE the main clause.
No, the subjects do not match.
Yes, both verbs share the subject Маша.
Yes, but only because выйдя is reflexive.
items.answer: Yes, both verbs share the subject Маша.
items.hint: Check the rule: same subject. Position is not part of the rule.
items.explanation: Маша is the subject of закрыла and of выйдя. The same-subject rule is satisfied. Gerund position (before or after the main clause) is a stylistic choice, not a grammatical constraint. The fourth option is wrong about the reason; выйдя is non-reflexive (выйти is the perfective infinitive).

items.promptEnglish: When I was approaching the house, it started to rain.
items.hint: The rain is not approaching the house: fix the dangling gerund.
items.explanation: A gerund must share its subject with the main clause, but дождь is not doing the approaching. The fix is a full когда clause: Когда я подходил к дому, начался дождь.

items.promptEnglish: When I was reading the newspaper, the phone rang.
items.hint: The phone is not reading: fix the dangling gerund.
items.explanation: The gerund Читая would claim the phone reads the paper. Russian requires the shared subject, so the correct version restores the когда clause: Когда я читал газету, зазвонил телефон.

items.promptEnglish: When I was opening the door, the vase fell.
items.hint: The vase is not opening anything.
items.explanation: Открывая would hang the gerund on ваза, which does no opening. The correct form is the full clause: Когда я открывал дверь, упала ваза - the gerund is only legal with a shared subject.

items.promptEnglish: When I had read the article, the doorbell rang.
items.hint: Perfective version of the same trap.
items.explanation: The doorbell did not read the article, so the gerund Прочитав dangles. The fix keeps the perfective meaning in a full clause: Когда я прочитал статью, раздался звонок.

fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Gerund forms attach to the subject of the main clause. Маша is that subject; only a gerund form can anchor the secondary action.
hints: Маша is the subject of посмотрела. Which form correctly attaches to her as a gerund clause?
explanations: Прочитав is the standard perfective gerund of прочитать; it shares the subject Маша with посмотрела. Прочитала is finite past tense and cannot anchor a gerund-style clause; прочитать is the infinitive; прочитавши is the older non-reflexive variant rarely used in modern Russian.

errorCorrection.sentence: Слушая музыку, раздался звонок в дверь.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: When I was listening to music, the doorbell rang.
errorCorrection.explanation: A verbal adverb must share its subject with the main verb, but the subject of раздался is звонок (the bell), and the doorbell is not listening to music, so the gerund Слушая dangles. Russian forbids this, so the fix is a когда clause with its own subject: Когда я слушал музыку. Послушав is the perfective gerund and still dangles, only changing the timing to a completed prior action, and Слушав is not a valid form. English tolerates 'Listening to music, the doorbell rang', but Russian does not.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: When I was reading the article, the phone rang.
errorCorrection.explanation: The same-subject rule requires the gerund and the main verb to share a doer, but the subject of зазвонил is телефон, and the phone is not reading the article, so Читая dangles. The repair is a когда clause that supplies its own human subject: Когда я читал статью. Прочитав is a perfective gerund that still dangles (and would change the meaning to a prior completed reading), and Читав статью is not a real gerund form. Russian cannot leave the gerund attached to a phantom subject the way casual English can.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: When I was sitting on the sofa, the light went out.
errorCorrection.explanation: A gerund attaches to the subject of the main clause, but here that subject is свет (the light), and the light is not sitting on the sofa, so Сидя dangles and the sentence is ungrammatical. The standard fix is a когда clause carrying its own subject: Когда я сидел на диване. Посидев is a perfective gerund that still dangles and shifts the timing to a completed prior action, while Сидев is not a valid form. Only the когда rewrite resolves the two-subject conflict.

minimalPairs.explanation: The subject of начался is дождь. The gerund Подходя would attach the approaching to the rain, which is wrong. The когда clause supplies the human subject (я) and preserves the timing relation. This is the canonical fix for a dangling gerund.

Антон is the subject of улыбнулся and узнав; the same-subject rule is satisfied, so the compact gerund is the natural choice. 'Когда узнал' would be grammatical but heavier, and Russian writing prefers the gerund when the subject is shared.

categorySorting.instruction: Sort each sentence by whether the same-subject rule is satisfied.

reviewVocab.definition: same-subject rule (the gerund and the main verb must share a subject; the most important rule for verbal adverbs)
reviewVocab.example: Гуляя по парку, мы говорили — общий субъект мы.

reviewVocab.definition: subject (the noun performing the verb's action; in the same-subject rule, both verbs share this noun)
когда clause (a finite subordinate clause with its own subject; the standard rewrite for a dangling gerund)
reviewVocab.example: *Подходя к дому, начался дождь → Когда я подходил к дому, начался дождь.

reviewVocab.definition: error (the most common verbal-adverb error in B2 writing is the dangling gerund: different subjects in main and gerund clauses)
